launches.title: Spur - testing infrastructure for your mobile apps
launches.tagline: test and validate your mobile apps in plain english.
launches.body:
hey everyone 👋 we're Sneha and Anushka, co-founders of [Spur](https://www.spurtest.com/).

### **TL;DR** Spur is building the validation infrastructure for software teams. We started with web testing, and today we're launching native app testing across iOS and Android.

Spur is building the validation infrastructure for software teams. We started with web testing, and today we're launching native app testing across iOS and Android.

Spur's agents test your apps the way real users do. You define the behavior you want to test in natural language, and Spur figures out how to execute and validate it across iOS and Android, native interactions, and web views.

Teams at HelloFresh, Nextdoor, DocuSign, Bilt, Alo Yoga, and Abercrombie are already using Spur for testing across their digital experience – on websites and on their apps.

**Our Ask:** If you’re building and maintaining a mobile app, we'd love to help you test it.\
Book a demo:[ https://spurtest.com/book-a-demo](https://spurtest.com/book-a-demo)

## **The problem**

Software is getting generated faster than ever: features that used to take days to build are now generated in minutes. But - once the feature exists, someone still has to figure out whether it actually works.

That validation process hasn't sped up at the same rate.

If you’re shipping mobile apps, this gets even harder. The same product flow often turns into separate automation for ios and android. Teams maintain the tests, the device infrastructure they run on, and the CI setup around them.

And as your product changes, your automation has to change with it.

## **The solution**

1. **Natural Language allows you to define the “intent” of a test:**

   Most test automation describes exactly _how_ to use an application.

   _Find this element. Tap it. Wait for another element. Enter text. Assert a value._

   That makes the test tightly coupled to the implementation. Spur tests describe what the user should be able _to do_ instead.

   _Add an item to cart, apply a promo code, and complete checkout with Apple Pay._

   The test captures the intent of the flow. Spur figures out how to execute it against the application in front of it. This means the same test can keep working across platforms or ui changes, because the thing you’re testing - the user behavior - hasn’t changed.
2. **Spur runs the infrastructure too**

   You upload the builds and choose what you want to validate. Spur handles the environment those tests execute in and runs them on our infrastructure. That means mobile testing becomes much closer to:

   _build → upload → validate_

   instead of becoming its own infrastructure project.

   Tests can run as part of a release, against a pull request, on a schedule, or whenever an engineer wants to validate a change.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116412&key=user_uploads/700570/52f7df91-1940-4f7c-a2df-4299adbee3e3)

3. **Built for engineers and agents**

   As more software is written by coding agents, we think validation also needs to become something agents can use directly.

   MCP is a first-class interface to Spur. A coding agent can make a change, ask Spur to validate the relevant user flows, inspect the result, fix what failed, and run the validation again.

   So the loop starts to look like:

   _generate → validate → fix → validate → ship_

   Humans can define the intent, using anything as context (tickets, figma files, PRDs, your codebase). Agents can continuously check whether the software still satisfies it.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116412&key=user_uploads/700570/1438d0de-f515-48cf-8f6c-4c478e4a7dba)


## **Why we built this**

We've spent the last few years building testing infrastructure for large software teams.

One thing has become increasingly clear: writing software is becoming dramatically easier, while proving that software works is still slow and expensive.

We think the gap between software generation and our ability to validate it is only going to widen.

The future of testing isn't maintaining more and more scripts. Validation needs to become more intelligent, adaptive, and be able to keep up with the rate at which software is changing.

That's what we're building at Spur.

If you're building or maintaining a mobile app, we'd love to work with you: <https://spurtest.com/book-a-demo>.

# **TL;DR: Spur lets you test your website with natural language.**

## You can launch web agents that mimic exactly what your users do on your platform, so you can ensure your product doesn’t fail your users.

---

### Launch Day Deal 🎉

As part of launch day, we are offering to help you set up tests for your **core flows** on [signup](https://tally.so/r/n9WR4Q) for free. \
Use the code `SPUR_LAUNCH` on signing up to redeem this deal.

—

# Here’s how it works! (A flow we test for the YC Tech Team)

An example test for YC’s Application Portal to Invite Co-Founders

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83237&key=user_uploads/700570/14e90a74-1b37-42e0-b36b-f6cc3b5d31aa)

<https://www.loom.com/share/bbab011b36904f4ea6d97a85225c7c30?sid=2023cab4-e476-4574-9ad3-f5daf34d4d89>

# **⛔️ The Problem (Do we even need to get into this?)**

A. Testing is TIME-CONSUMING and PAINFUL. 🤕

* whether you write a test
* or manually check (or maybe not check) your core flows every single time you merge to production

B. Tests are not MAINTAINABLE; they break! 🛠️

* Your UI is constantly changing, and maintaining test scripts is a tedious task.

## **✨ The Solution**

On Spur, you can:

* Write automated tests in minutes (_not hours_) with natural language 💨💨
* Not worry about maintaining tests when your UI changes 💅

  _We use multimodal agents that interact with your web pages exactly like users would. Tests are not bound to CSS selectors_

## **🧡 The Team behind Spur**

[Anushka](https://linkedin.com/in/anushka-nijhawan-8380361b1) and I met our freshman year at Yale. We did research at the Yale NLP Lab on web agents. [Sneha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sivakumarsneha/) (here!) previously worked on growth at Figma, and Anushka at DeepMind. We’ve hacked on our fair share of projects before — and have very much felt the pain of neglecting testing.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83237&key=user_uploads/700570/6ceb23f3-b013-4f80-a2f0-04e4c1539ba3)

## **🤝 Our Ask**

### **If this problem is one that you face, try us out!**

* Book a [demo](https://calendly.com/sneha-sivakumar-1/30min)
* [Sign up!](https://tally.so/r/n9WR4Q) We are live and actively onboarding customers every single day

Our customers have found a **lot** of value from using us so far, and we’d love to take testing off your plate. Here is what some of them have said :)

> Spur is shockingly easy to use—no coding, just plain English. Simply describe what you want to test, and Spur handles the rest. Onboarding was a breeze, and Anushka and Sneha are fantastic to work with.
>
> _\- Eve Bouffard, Product Engineer @ YC Tech Team_

> I’m gonna see if I can expense Spur through my wellness stipend. Category: Therapy\
> \- Gabe Wilson, Founder & CTO @ Terrakotta

> We had a HUGE UI revamp and are still able to test easily without needing maintenance, not a single test has broken due to flakiness. They mean it when they say their tests are reliable. \
> \- Joseph Parker, Founder & CTO @ VecFlow

> We’ve been using Spur and it’s been AMAZING — unlike all the competitors that we’ve tried, they actually work! Can highly recommend.\
> \- Konsti Wohlwend, Founder @ StackAuth
